subject: Apex RFI: Migration acceptance criteria, data-retention sequence & fallback lanes
messages:
From: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@apexfinancial.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, procurement@apexfinancial.com
Cc: Melissa Tan <melissa.tan@apexfinancial.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: Migration acceptance criteria & data-retention sequencing

Kim — thanks for the draft RFI packet. A few implementation details we need clarified for our SOC/compliance board and migration committee before we can proceed to vendor selection: 

1) Acceptance criteria: please provide explicit pass/fail criteria for the pilot and production cutover (including SLA targets, error budgets, and sample evaluation prompts we can run).
2) Data retention sequence: during migration we will keep historical conversational logs for 90 days in staging before full migration. Confirm how Redwood handles prefix/KV cache invalidation and whether we can enforce a per-tenant retention window during phased migration.
3) Fallback lanes: detail automatic fallback behavior if the dedicated pool hits capacity (what model variants are used, latency degradation profile, and how state is preserved).
4) Rollback: steps to return to the legacy endpoint if we detect regressions within the first 48 hours of production traffic. 

Can you return a short document (1–2 pages) with acceptance tests and an annotated timeline that maps to our internal gates? We have a procurement review on 5-Nov; would be ideal to get this by Nov 3.

Thanks,
Sam
Samuel Ortiz
Technical Program Manager — Migrations
Apex Financial

Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Migration acceptance criteria & data-retention sequencing

Sam — appreciate the clear asks. We'll pull together a concise response that maps directly to your gates and include an annotated timeline and rollback checklist. Quick notes:

- We can provide explicit acceptance tests (SLOs + sample prompt set).
- Tenant-level retention policy is supported via our Private deployment (VPC) and Dedicated controls; we'll document the KV cache invalidation window and retention enforcement steps.
- Fallback lanes: default behavior is configurable; we will supply latency degradation estimates and exact model variants used for auto-fallback.

I'll circulate an internal draft tomorrow and send the client-facing 2-page summary by Nov 3. Looping in our migration lead and solutions architect to confirm technical details (internal).

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Apex RFI — draft acceptance criteria & timeline (please review)

Team — Samuel asked for a 1–2 page deliverable for procurement. I attached my working materials (Apex_RFI_Migration_QA.xlsx and a PDF schedule). Please review the items below and add notes inline in the sheet: 

Key asks to cover:
- Pilot acceptance (week 0–2): functional correctness thresholds (token-level hallucination <2% on sampled prompts, end-to-end P99 latency <450ms for critical routes), and sample eval prompts (sheet tab: "Pilot Prompts").
- Pre-prod validation (week 3–4): golden traffic replay (1% of production), integration smoke tests (schema checks, auth handshakes), and audit log completeness (no missing request IDs).
- Production cutover (week 5): canary -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over three days with gating rules. Must include automated rollback triggers (error rate >1.5% for 30m or latency >2x baseline).
- Data retention: describe KV cache TTLs, steps to export logs to customer-managed S3 for the 90-day window, and a retention enforcement command to purge caches per-tenant.
- Fallback lanes: explicit mapping (Dedicated -> Hostpool-compatible quantized variant -> Hosted burst). Include expected tail-latency delta and token-cost delta per lane.

Action items:
- Aditya: confirm feasibility of per-tenant purge command and retention enforcement steps; add exact CLI/API calls.
- Marissa: fill in deployment cadence and SRE runbook pointers; attach rollback-checklist.md.
- Rishi: add precise model variant names and expected latency/cost numbers for each fallback lane.

I'll incorporate edits and produce the client-facing 2-pager by Nov 3.

Thanks — Kim
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 15:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Apex RFI — draft acceptance criteria & timeline (please review)

Kim — quick tech notes (added to sheet):

- Per-tenant retention/purge: implemented as a namespaced KV purge endpoint (POST /admin/tenants/{id}/kv/purge) — requires org-admin scope and logs an irreversible retention event. We can schedule staggered purges during the final day of sync.
- KV cache invalidation: TTLs are configurable; during migration we recommend setting prefix TTL to 10m for staging and 24h for pre-prod to avoid cold-start spike. We'll document the exact sequence for invalidation (invalidate prefix -> flush local cache -> warm with replay traffic).
- Fallback lanes: recommended mapping: dedicated-pool (Apex-dedicated-v1) -> quantized-xq8 variant (apex-xq8-compatible) -> hosted-n1-small for burst. Latency deltas: +40–80ms to quantized variant; hosted burst adds +150–300ms depending on region. Token cost delta estimates included in sheet.
- Rollback automation: we can wire an automatic rollback play if: 1) error_rate > 1.5% for 30m OR 2) data-regression detected on sampled prompts (we'll run the prompt-suite every 15m during canary). Rollback executes: traffic shift to legacy endpoint (weighted 0.0 -> 100% within 20 minutes) + alerting + postmortem stub.

I'll attach the CLI examples and runbook snippets into the draft before EOD.

- Adi
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@apexfinancial.com>, Melissa Tan <melissa.tan@apexfinancial.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Apex — Migration acceptance criteria and fallback lanes (deliverable)

Sam / Melissa — attached is the 2-page summary you requested plus supporting artifacts. Highlights below (we mapped to your procurement gates):

Pilot (weeks 0–2) — Acceptance tests:
- Functional pass: sample prompt-suite (attached) must have <2% hallucination on domain-sensitive prompts and >95% intent-match on routing tests.
- Performance pass: P95 < 300ms, P99 < 450ms for critical endpoints under pilot load (observed with 10 concurrent clients).

Pre-prod (weeks 3–4) — Validation:
- Golden replay: run 1% production traffic replay; no more than 0.2% request-ID loss across logs.
- Integration: schema handshake (versioned contract), OAuth token rotation test, end-to-end tracing.

Production cutover (week 5) — Rollout cadence & automated gates:
- Canary 0–5% (6h), 5–25% (24h), 25–100% (48h).
- Automated rollback triggers: error_rate > 1.5% sustained for 30m OR prompt-suite regression >1.5% on sampled set.

Data retention & KV sequence:
- Tenant-level retention enforced via admin purge endpoint. Recommended staging retention = 90d export to customer S3; pre-prod use 24h KV TTL; production default remains as contract.
- Invalidation sequence: invalidate prefix -> flush local shards -> warm caches with replayed requests (script included in rollback-checklist.md).

Fallback lanes (explicit mapping):
- Primary: Apex-dedicated-v1 (full-precision)
- Fallthrough 1: apex-xq8-compatible (quantized, moderate accuracy tradeoff) — latency +40–80ms, token-cost -18%
- Fallthrough 2: hosted-burst-n1 (fast, higher latency) — latency +150–300ms, token-cost +5–10%

Attachments included: Apex_RFI_Migration_QA.xlsx (detailed gates & numbers), redwood-migration-schedule-v2.pdf (timeline & windows), rollback-checklist.md (runbook snippets + CLI).

Next steps: please confirm by Nov 5 if the acceptance tests and fallback mapping are sufficient for procurement. If you want, we can do a 30–45 minute technical walkthrough next week to walk through CLI examples and the prompt-suite.

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment stubs: Apex_RFI_Migration_QA.xlsx (xlsx), redwood-migration-schedule-v2.pdf (pdf), rollback-checklist.md (text)
From: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@apexfinancial.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Melissa Tan <melissa.tan@apexfinancial.com>, procurement@apexfinancial.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 17:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Apex — Migration acceptance criteria and fallback lanes (deliverable)

Kim — this is exactly what procurement wanted, thank you. A couple of quick clarifications before we mark as final: 

1) For the automated rollback, can you reduce the traffic-shift window to 10 minutes (from 20) for the initial canary? Our ops team prefers faster reverts for customer-facing flows. Will that increase the risk of in-flight request loss?
2) For the apex-xq8-compatible variant, can you call out any known regression classes (e.g., numeric precision on financial prompts, date parsing) so our QA can focus tests?

If you can confirm those two items by EOD Nov 9 we'll move this into the procurement packet. Otherwise we can accept as-is but will request the faster rollback window as a concession in contract.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.
Sam
